chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah and Ubayd ibn Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Any man who has crops or fruit and gives its zakat is not obliged to pay anything in it if the year passes while it is in his possession, unless he converts it into capital wealth; and if he does so and the year passes while it is in his possession, he must pay its zakat, otherwise there is no obligation upon him even if it remains for a thousand years, provided it remains in its original form. He is only obliged to pay the tithe (zakat al-'ushr). If he pays it once, there is no obligation upon him until it is converted into capital wealth and the year passes while it is in his possession."
The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: As for the livestock, zakat is obligatory upon them specifically only if they are sa'imah (grazing in pastures) and the year passes over them.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in zakat obligation between agricultural produce kept for consumption versus converted into capital wealth?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between *Ushr* (tithe) on agricultural produce and *Zakat* on wealth (*mal*), establishing that conversion to capital triggers the lunar year (*hawl*) requirement for full zakat. It reflects the Shia juristic view that raw produce is exempt from zakat until sold or stored as wealth, while the Sheikh’s note on livestock highlights the specific condition of free-grazing (*sa'imah*) for zakat obligation. This ruling underscores the principle that zakat is a tax on accumulated capital rather than a levy on natural yield itself.
